openings.claim: Future capability: volunteers recognize a sealed kit’s assigned pattern and a single missing shared-material item by its tactile paper-stack signature, without opening it. This would support complete, correctly assigned kits for participants while shortening the volunteers’ checking burden; no such benefit is established.
openings.delta: Existing sample kits become physical reference signatures for closed-envelope comparison, rather than occasionally consulted visual recipes. The currently testable enabling capability is blind discrimination of otherwise matched complete and one-item-short envelopes; merely recognizing grossly different pattern sizes does not qualify.
openings.prediction: With identifying marks concealed, a volunteer using existing samples as references correctly judges both pattern and completeness for at least 11 of 12 randomized envelopes, including at least five of six one-item omissions. Results survive a fresh shuffled presentation with new concealed codes.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is gross bulk recognition: envelope feel distinguishes some patterns but dampens single-sheet differences. Pattern judgments may succeed while matched complete-versus-omission judgments remain near chance.
openings.defeat: Repeated confusion between matched complete and one-item-short envelopes defeats the enabling capability even if pattern recognition succeeds. A subsequent 60-kit trial exceeding 90 minutes or requiring more than one distribution correction defeats operational usefulness.
openings.probe: Within one two-volunteer, 90-minute session, prepare 12 temporary envelopes using the actual pattern mixture and available shared materials: six complete and six matched single-item omissions. One volunteer records concealed ground truth; the other, blinded, feels each envelope against sample references and records judgments. Shuffle and recode for a second pass. Restore every recipe before distribution. Handle envelopes sequentially on the existing table.
assumptions: Envelope paper transmits repeatable differences despite pressure and packing variation; this is unverified.
Existing supplies suffice for reusable probe envelopes and reference comparisons without purchases.
Preparation, blinding, testing and restoration fit 90 minutes with exactly two volunteers.
The probe evaluates discrimination only; reliable 60-kit throughput and table fit remain unproven.
